notes: Inbound SMB lead — discovered via blog post on prompt compression. Self-serve sign-up first week of Feb.
Primary contact: Mariela Torres (CTO). Quote from call: 'We love the dev DX but monthly spend is creeping — need pragmatic ops levers.'
Main ask: reduce per-session token spend without degrading UX. Interested in batching, prefix KV caching, and prompt compression layers.
Usage profile: conversational support sessions (avg session 6 turns), occasional bulk embeddings for search reindexing (daily batch).
Latency expectation: p95 < 400ms for reg-support messages; can accept slightly higher for non-interactive batch jobs.
Model preference: leaning toward smaller quantized open models for cost (13B quantized) but wants Redwood to show tradeoffs vs hosted larger models.
Cost sensitivity: budget cap ~ $600/mo initially; willing to expand if clear ROI on deflection and response quality.
Notes on analytics: asked for token audit of last 30 days, wants breakdown by endpoint, average tokens per prompt and per completion.
Operational constraints: public cloud ok, no on-prem requirement; require SOC2 attestation and optional SSO later.
SE input: recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated greetings, compress system prompts, and autosuggest batch window of 50ms to catch micro-batching without UX hit.
